concepts.def: An amount of substance containing 6.02 × 10²³ particles
Relative atomic mass of an element
Relative formula mass — sum of Ar values in a formula
Total mass before a reaction equals total mass after
Same number of each atom on both sides

walkthroughs.body_html:
Atoms are tiny, so chemists count them in moles.

1 mole = 6.02 × 10²³ particles. That huge number is called the Avogadro constant.

Whether you have 1 mole of carbon or 1 mole of water, you have the same number of particles.

Ar is the relative atomic mass of an element — you read it off the periodic table.

Mr is the relative formula mass. Just add up the Ar of every atom in the formula.

Example: H₂O has Mr = 1 + 1 + 16 = 18.

Atoms aren't created or destroyed in a reaction — they just rearrange.

So total mass before = total mass after.

That's why equations must be balanced: the same atoms appear on both sides, just bonded differently.

mcqs.q: How many particles are in 1 mole of any substance?
Why must a chemical equation be balanced?
options: Because mass is conserved — atoms aren't lost or made
So the products always weigh more

numericals.q: What is the Mr of CaCO₃? (Ca=40, C=12, O=16)

free_texts.q: What is the Mr of NaCl? (Na=23, Cl=35.5). Give a number only.
